scope: Corollary 4.7 (Equal-offset moments with varying separations) of the manuscript “The Gaussian free field limit of integer Lipschitz heights with two-arc boundary data” (preprints/The-Gaussian-free-field-limit-of-integer-Lipschitz-heights-with-two-arc-boundary-data-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0047faf78711628), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For a nonempty obstacle family in the preceding setup, impose the additional event E = {ti = t1 for every i}. The obstacles may now vary or approach one another, while staying away from a fixed test disk. Fix an annular buffer around that disk, with positive clearance from the disk and with fixed inner and outer radii. Suppose the buffer and its filled interior contain no pins. Suppose that, under conditioning on the pins and E, an exterior search finds a surrounding double-B cut in this buffer, with probability at least c > 0 uniformly in the varying arrangements. Suppose that E can be checked in the exterior of the selected cut, so its strict interior remains free given the trace. Then the zero-total test in that disk has moments bounded uniformly in those arrangements. A sufficient condition is that the cut probability conditional on the pins alone is at least c0 > 0, that P(E | pins) → 1 uniformly along the varying family, and that the same exterior measurability holds.
